intent: Build a free, open-source Typeless alternative.

productReference.name: Typeless
productReference.role: Commercial product reference for the open-source alternative idea.

summary: The precedent set shows this should be a full voice-to-polished-text workflow, not a simple Whisper wrapper.

candidates.name: Open-Less/openless
candidates.evidence: Closest full-product reference: hotkey recording, ASR, LLM polish, style packs, cursor insertion, settings, and local-first positioning.
takeaways: Study the full product loop before designing the MVP.
Treat polished text as the core value, not raw transcription.
Use as the first hands-on product reference.
risks: Do not copy implementation without checking exact files and notices.

candidates.name: TypeWhisper/typewhisper-mac
candidates.evidence: Strong macOS-native reference for local engines, privacy, WhisperKit, and optional cloud support.
takeaways: Borrow local-engine and privacy architecture ideas.
Study plugin/engine boundaries if building macOS-first.
risks: GPL-3.0 means direct code reuse needs license compatibility review.

candidates.name: hehehai/voxt
candidates.evidence: Useful reference for app-specific and URL-specific prompt rules, translation, and menu-bar voice workflows.
takeaways: Borrow the app-aware prompt routing idea.
Study how different apps get different enhancement behavior.
risks: License needs review before direct reuse.

candidates.name: never13254/GhostType
candidates.evidence: Low-star but conceptually sharp context-aware Typeless alternative with prompt presets and app detection.
takeaways: Use as proof that low-star repos can still be high-signal.
risks: Validate implementation maturity before relying on it.

candidates.name: DoodzProg/AcouZ
candidates.evidence: Small Windows-focused reference for hold-key, speak, release, and insert-into-any-app behavior.
takeaways: Use as a Windows MVP reference.
Study platform-specific hotkey and insertion behavior.
risks: May not be mature enough as primary architecture reference.

use: Use OpenLess as the closest full-product reference and first hands-on comparison.
borrow: Borrow TypeWhisper's local/private engine architecture ideas.
Borrow Voxt and GhostType's app-aware prompt routing and context presets.
Borrow AcouZ as a minimal Windows workflow reference.
avoid: Avoid building only a Whisper wrapper.
Avoid treating transcription as the final product instead of the first step in a writing workflow.
buildNew: Build new only with a clear differentiated focus, such as coding-agent prompt dictation or a simpler cross-platform open-source workflow.

credits.name: Open-Less/openless
credits.credit: Closest full-product precedent for the Typeless alternative idea.
credits.reuseGuidance: Permissive license; preserve notices and verify exact files before direct reuse.

credits.name: TypeWhisper/typewhisper-mac
credits.credit: Reference for local-first macOS engine and privacy architecture.
credits.reuseGuidance: Treat as architecture inspiration unless GPL compatibility is intended.

credits.name: hehehai/voxt
credits.credit: Reference for app-aware prompt routing and voice translation workflow.
credits.reuseGuidance: License needs review; borrow ideas only until verified.

credits.name: never13254/GhostType
credits.credit: Reference for context-aware Typeless replacement positioning.
credits.reuseGuidance: Permissive license; verify exact files before direct reuse.

credits.name: DoodzProg/AcouZ
credits.credit: Reference for a minimal Windows voice dictation path.
credits.reuseGuidance: Permissive license; verify exact files before direct reuse.

nextImplementationConstraints: Model the product as a pipeline: record audio -> ASR -> text polish -> style/mode routing -> insert at cursor.
Keep ASR provider, LLM provider, style presets, dictionary, history, and insertion as separate modules.
Test the real hotkey-to-cursor workflow in target apps, not just isolated transcription.
Make license and credits visible in README or implementation notes when precedents shape the product.
